title: SEC1: TLS acceptor loaded per-connection, cert errors not caught at startup
description: In lifecycle.rs, both run_session (NNTPS, line 64) and run_plain_session (STARTTLS, line 143) call load_tls_acceptor() on every accepted TCP connection. A broken cert (wrong path, bad PEM, mismatched key) is only discovered when the first client connects, not at server startup. The warn\! log at that point is per-connection, not a startup error. In production, a cert rotation that corrupts the file will silently accept TCP connections and then fail every TLS handshake with 'TLS acceptor setup failed' — potentially for minutes before an operator notices the warn log stream. The acceptor should be built once at startup (or validated at startup with a fast-fail error), and the result passed into the session handlers.
